sentences.text: Stenopelix was a small herbivore that lived approximately 140 million years ago in Europe during the Berriasian stage.
This bipedal dinosaur grew to about 1.5 meters in length and stood roughly 0.7 meters tall, weighing around 10 kilograms.
Because the skull is missing, scientists classify the animal based on unique hip features, such as an ilium shaft that tapers to a rounded point and an ischium shaft with a distinctive kink.
The known fossil consists of hollow impressions on two non-overlapping plates, which researchers have used to create gypsum and latex casts for study.
The genus name translates to 'narrow pelvis,' a description derived from Greek words.
A fossil was found in 1855 in a sandstone quarry near Bückeburg, Germany, and Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer named the species Stenopelix valdensis in 1857.
The classification of Stenopelix remains controversial and problematic due to the lack of a skull.
In 1974, Teresa Maryańska suggested the animal belonged to the pachycephalosaurians, one of the oldest known groups, based on specific pelvic and rib characteristics.
However, Peter Galton later showed that the structure previously thought to be a pubis was actually part of the hip socket, leading him to conclude the animal was a ceratopsian.
Later analyses by Paul Sereno placed Stenopelix within the Pachycephalosauria again.

Richard J. Butler and Robert M. Sullivan rejected these earlier identifications, viewing the animal as a marginocephalian of uncertain position, while a 2011 study by Butler et al. showed it is a basal ceratopsian related to Yinlong, now classified in the family Chaoyangsauridae.
Stenopelix lived between 139.1 and 137.05 million years ago.
